qr_tiny: warp-per-matrix lane-owns-column kernel for n<=32, SINGLE launch. Lane c owns column c in 32 private registers; unblocked Householder fully in registers (no smem matrix, no HBM round-trips). Brief small-GEMM-overhead-exceeds-scalar-saving confirmed.

Static-indexed float[16] arrays (no local-mem spill). Larger panels (L>512) keep the plain 2-read loop since a 128-chunk cache would spill. n512 8804 (-1.6%, 4 dominant shapes), n4096 58041 (-5.0%); n1024 ~flat (1024-thread blocks are register-starved). Now ALL NT threads reduce their stripe of the column norm (warp-shuffle then block-sum via sw) and write their stripe of sv; every thread recomputes the uniform reflector scalars (alpha read before any overwrite, no broadcast). Precision is NOT the lever; the structural wall is occupancy (full-height smem residency) + trailing parallelism (one CTA/matrix). The BEST CUDA mega needs the COOPERATIVE multi-CTA-per-matrix design (grid=(G,B) per-matrix barrier: G CTAs cooperatively factor the panel then parallelize the trailing col-strips) to restore parallelism. Building that next.

Committed as the decisive NEGATIVE (444f9cd0, QR_MEGA_IMPL=coop default off). Best validating megakernel = Triton 1-CTA (2546us); setting it as the live mega default.
